bibliographic.title: Designing and evaluating large language model-enabled clinical decision support for heart failure: a modular and risk-tiered framework
bibliographic.authors: Zhu W, Peng J, Yan Z, Chen Y, Xu J, Zhang L
bibliographic.citation_apa: Zhu, W., Peng, J., Yan, Z., Chen, Y., Xu, J., & Zhang, L. (2026). Designing and evaluating large language model-enabled clinical decision support for heart failure: A modular and risk-tiered framework. Frontiers in Digital Health, 8, 1730457. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2026.1730457

methodology.study_design: perspective article proposing modular risk-tiered design and evaluation framework (HF-IA)
methodology.technology_context: LLM-enabled clinical decision support for heart failure; retrieval-augmented generation; modular agent functions; electronic health record integration; risk-tiered autonomy

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed conceptual perspective on governance, design, and evaluation of LLM-enabled clinical decision support in regulated heart-failure care. It directly addresses LLMs, clinical governance, risk-tiered autonomy, RAG, and post-deployment monitoring, but it is not primarily about conversational governance of chatbots or dialogue systems and does not report an implemented conversational product or empirical conversational evaluation.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction were provided; full framework sections on governance, oversight, and monitoring may alter conversational-governance coding and appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate as a conceptual governance/design framework rather than empirical study. Authors explicitly state the work is conceptual, not an implemented software product, and not a systematic review. Sampling and data-collection criteria are weakly applicable because no primary dataset or participant sample is reported in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is clearly articulated and internally coherent for LLM-enabled HF clinical decision support governance, but confidence is moderated because the provided excerpt contains no empirical validation, no full operational governance specification, and limited direct evidence on conversational oversight mechanisms.

coding.theme: Risk-tiered governance and evaluation of LLM-enabled clinical decision support
coding.subtheme: Modular HF intelligent agent framework embedded in clinical governance
rq_alignment: governance of generative AI in regulated settings

synthesis.main_claim: HF-specific LLM clinical decision support should be designed as a modular, risk-tiered framework (HF-IA) rather than a single autonomous agent, with evaluation combining node-level tests, longitudinal case replay, silent prospective validation, and post-deployment monitoring within clinical governance.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a disease-specific conceptual framework clarifying design, evaluation, and governance requirements for future LLM-enabled heart failure decision support, including RAG and differentiated risk levels across agent functions.
synthesis.limitations: Conceptual only; does not claim clinical effectiveness; not an implemented software product; not a systematic review of LLM cardiology applications; provided excerpt does not establish conversational-system governance empirically.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for governance patterns in regulated LLM clinical systems, especially modular risk-tiering, validation pathways, RAG integration, and post-deployment monitoring; treat as foundational context for healthcare CDS rather than central evidence on conversational governance.
